questions.question: What is retrieval-augmented generation?
questions.reference_answer: A technique that retrieves relevant passages from a collection and places them in the prompt so the model answers from supplied evidence rather than memory.

questions.question: How is a RAG system's indexing stage different from its query stage?
questions.reference_answer: Indexing runs ahead of time as a batch job that loads, cleans, splits, encodes and stores documents; querying runs per request and must be fast.

questions.question: Why do all my documents look similar when I compare their embeddings?
questions.reference_answer: Cosine scores are only meaningful relative to the model in use, and shared boilerplate text pulls every vector toward a common direction.

questions.question: Should I normalise vectors before computing cosine similarity?
questions.reference_answer: Dividing each vector by its magnitude makes the dot product equal the cosine, which is faster; it fails on zero vectors produced by empty input.

questions.question: How should I split documents before embedding them?
questions.reference_answer: Pick a strategy (fixed, sentence-aware or paragraph-aware), add ten to twenty percent overlap, and tune the size against an evaluation set.

questions.question: What chunk size should I use?
questions.reference_answer: There is no universal value; sweep a few sizes against a labelled question set. Small pieces match sharply but lose context, large ones dilute the match.

questions.question: How do I read a file one chunk at a time in Python?
questions.reference_answer: Iterate over the file object for lines, or call read(size) for a bounded number of characters, so memory stays flat.

questions.question: How large should an audio chunk be when reading a wave file?
questions.reference_answer: A whole number of frames; multiply the frame count by sample width and channel count to get the byte length.

questions.question: Why does my chunking loop never finish?
questions.reference_answer: The overlap is greater than or equal to the chunk size, so the window never advances.

questions.question: What is BM25 and when does it fail?
questions.reference_answer: A lexical ranker that weights rare terms and corrects for length; it is blind to a question phrased entirely in synonyms.

questions.question: What is the difference between lexical and semantic search?
questions.reference_answer: Lexical matches surface forms and excels at exact strings; semantic compares meaning in vector space and handles paraphrase.

questions.question: How do I combine keyword and vector search, and how do I pick the weight?
questions.reference_answer: Normalise both result lists to a common range, blend with a weight, and sweep that weight on a labelled question set.

questions.question: How does reciprocal rank fusion work?
questions.reference_answer: Each list contributes one over a constant plus the item's rank, summed per item; only positions are used so no score normalisation is needed.

questions.question: How can I improve the ordering of my retrieved results?
questions.reference_answer: Over-fetch candidates cheaply, then score each query-passage pair with a cross-encoder and keep the best few.

questions.question: Why can't a reranker fix a passage that retrieval never returned?
questions.reference_answer: Recall is fixed by the first stage; the reranker only reorders the candidates it is given.

questions.question: Why is a two-stage retrieval pipeline cheaper than scoring the whole index?
questions.reference_answer: Narrow to a small candidate set with a cheap method first, then spend the expensive, more accurate method only on the survivors.

questions.question: Why does the model make things up when it doesn't know?
questions.reference_answer: Given no relevant passages it falls back on training patterns and fills the gap; instruct it to decline and verify each claim against the supplied passages.

questions.question: How do I generate alternative phrasings of a user's question?
questions.reference_answer: Produce a paraphrase, a version in domain terminology, a keyword-only version and a hypothetical answer, then search each and merge.

questions.question: How do I deduplicate results when searching with several query variations?
questions.reference_answer: Merge on the passage identifier and keep the best rank achieved across the formulations.

questions.question: How many passages should I pass to the model?
questions.reference_answer: Three to five is a common operating point; over-fetch then filter by score or rerank rather than retrieving few directly.

questions.question: How do I stop the prompt from exceeding the context limit?
questions.reference_answer: Reserve the output allowance first, divide the remainder among passages, and drop whole low-ranked passages rather than truncating every one.

questions.question: How do I count tokens to estimate cost?
questions.reference_answer: Count with the same tokeniser the target model uses; token counts do not map cleanly onto word counts and providers bill per token.

questions.question: How do I make a RAG answer cite its sources?
questions.reference_answer: Keep identifier, path and position with each passage, label them in the prompt, instruct the model to cite the labels, and verify the labels it emitted.

questions.question: What should the instruction in an augmented prompt say?
questions.reference_answer: State that the answer must come from the supplied passages and that the model should say it does not know when they do not contain one.

questions.question: Can a retrieved document contain instructions that hijack the model?
questions.reference_answer: Yes. Retrieved text joins the prompt, so mark it as untrusted data, state it must not be obeyed, and limit what the system can do.

questions.question: How should API keys be handled in a deployed application?
questions.reference_answer: Load them from environment variables or a managed secret store, never commit them, and redact them from logs.

questions.question: What metadata should I store alongside each passage?
questions.reference_answer: Source, section, position and identifier, kept as flat scalars so the store can filter on them before comparing similarity.

questions.question: Why does my filtered search return nothing?
questions.reference_answer: The metadata clause matched no items; report how many survived the filter to separate 'nothing relevant' from 'nothing eligible'.

questions.question: How do I make a Chroma collection survive a restart?
questions.reference_answer: Create the client with a persistence path so the collection is written to disk.

questions.question: Do I have to re-index when I change embedding model?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; vectors from different models are not comparable, so the whole collection must be re-encoded.

questions.question: How does an approximate nearest neighbour index avoid comparing everything?
questions.reference_answer: It walks layers of linked neighbours greedily toward the query, examining only a small fraction of the collection.

questions.question: How do I measure whether my retrieval is any good?
questions.reference_answer: Recall@k tells you whether the correct source was found at all; a rank-sensitive measure such as MRR tells you whether it was placed early.

questions.question: How many questions do I need in an evaluation set, and what should they cover?
questions.reference_answer: Thirty to fifty spanning simple lookups, multi-source questions, unusual phrasings, and questions the collection cannot answer.

questions.question: How do I tell whether a change to my pipeline actually helped?
questions.reference_answer: Vary one factor at a time on the same questions and metric, seed any randomness, and report per-question outcomes alongside the aggregate.

questions.question: How do I judge whether an answer is correct without exact string matching?
questions.reference_answer: Check for required key facts, or use a model as judge while auditing a sample by hand.

questions.question: How can I expose a RAG system through an HTTP API?
questions.reference_answer: Declare request models for validation, load expensive objects once in a lifespan handler, and keep blocking calls off the event loop.

questions.question: How do I show the answer while it is still being generated?
questions.reference_answer: Stream tokens over server-sent events; errors after the first byte must be carried as an event since the status code is already sent.

questions.question: Why does my Streamlit chat history disappear?
questions.reference_answer: The script re-runs on every interaction, so values must be kept in session state rather than local variables.

questions.question: How should I containerise this application?
questions.reference_answer: Pin the base image, install requirements before copying source so the layer cache works, and mount model and vector data rather than baking it in.

questions.question: What should I log for each request?
questions.reference_answer: Question, rewrites, passage identifiers and scores, token usage, per-stage latency and the final answer.

questions.question: What should I cache in a RAG system?
questions.reference_answer: Embeddings keyed on a hash of the text, retrieval results per normalised question, and completions with care.

questions.question: How should I handle being rate limited by the provider?
questions.reference_answer: Retry with exponential backoff and jitter up to a capped number of attempts, and never retry a malformed request.

questions.question: How do I embed a large number of documents efficiently?
questions.reference_answer: Send batches in one call, split on a running token count, and retry failures with backoff while recording what already succeeded.

questions.question: Should I use a hosted or a local embedding model?
questions.reference_answer: Hosted costs per call and needs a key; local is free per call and private but needs setup and memory. Decide with a small labelled set from your own corpus.

questions.question: Is RAG the right approach for counting how many records match a condition?
questions.reference_answer: No. Only a handful of passages are consulted, so aggregation over an entire collection belongs in a database query.

questions.question: What does an embedding actually represent?
questions.reference_answer: A fixed-length vector whose geometric relationship to other vectors encodes similarity of meaning; individual coordinates are not interpretable.

questions.question: What does a vector database give me over a plain list of vectors?
questions.reference_answer: It stores text and metadata alongside the vectors and answers nearest-neighbour queries without comparing against every row.

questions.question: Why does mutating a default list argument cause bugs?
questions.reference_answer: Defaults are evaluated once at definition time, so one shared object accumulates state between calls; default to None instead.

questions.question: How do I stop garbled characters appearing in extracted text?
questions.reference_answer: Pass encoding='utf-8' explicitly rather than relying on the platform default.

questions.question: What is the cleanest way to define a record type that holds named fields?
questions.reference_answer: A dataclass, using default_factory for mutable defaults and frozen=True when the instance must be hashable.

questions.question: How should I structure try and except blocks?
questions.reference_answer: Wrap the smallest failing region, name the specific exception, use else for the success path and finally for cleanup, and re-raise bare to keep the traceback.

questions.question: Why should each project get its own virtual environment?
questions.reference_answer: It isolates installed packages from the system interpreter; pinned requirements make the install reproducible.

questions.question: Why does indentation matter in Python?
questions.reference_answer: Indentation is syntax: it marks the body of a block, and mixing tabs with spaces raises a TabError.

questions.question: What is the difference between learning from labelled and unlabelled data?
questions.reference_answer: Supervised learning fits input-output pairs against a recorded answer; unsupervised learning optimises an objective defined only over the inputs.

questions.question: My training score keeps improving but my test score doesn't. What is happening?
questions.reference_answer: The model is overfitting: it is memorising noise specific to the training set.

questions.question: Why is attention expensive on long inputs?
questions.reference_answer: Attention compares every pair of positions, so cost grows with the square of sequence length.

questions.question: Why is TF-IDF high for some words and not others?
questions.reference_answer: The weight is high for a term frequent in this document and rare across the collection.

questions.question: How do I keep my chunks from cutting sentences in half?
questions.reference_answer: Use sentence-aware chunking, accumulating whole sentences until the next one would exceed the target size.

questions.question: Where should chunk size and result count be configured?
questions.reference_answer: Outside the source, read from the environment with defaults, and validated at startup so a bad value fails immediately.
